title: Part 67 & 68: Medical Standards
description: Understand medical certificate classes, requirements, durations, and BasicMed from 14 CFR Parts 67 and 68

questions.question: Which class of medical certificate has the most stringent requirements?
options: All classes have the same requirements
questions.explanation: First class medical certificates have the most stringent requirements, as they are required for airline transport pilots.

questions.question: What is the duration of a first class medical certificate for a pilot under age 40?
questions.explanation: For pilots under 40, a first class medical is valid for 12 calendar months for first class privileges, then continues as second/third class.

questions.question: What is the duration of a third class medical certificate for a pilot under age 40?
questions.explanation: For pilots under 40, a third class medical is valid for 60 calendar months (5 years).

questions.question: What is the duration of a third class medical certificate for a pilot age 40 or older?
questions.explanation: For pilots 40 or older, a third class medical is valid for 24 calendar months.

questions.question: Which medical certificate class is required for private pilot privileges?
questions.explanation: Private pilot privileges require at least a third class medical certificate (or BasicMed).

questions.question: What is the minimum distant visual acuity standard for a third class medical?
options: 20/40 or better in each eye separately, with or without correction
questions.explanation: Third class medical requires 20/40 or better distant vision in each eye separately, with or without corrective lenses.

questions.question: What is the minimum near vision standard for a third class medical?
questions.explanation: Third class medical requires 20/40 or better near vision at 16 inches, with or without corrective lenses.

questions.question: Under BasicMed, how often must a pilot complete the online medical education course?
questions.explanation: BasicMed requires completion of the online medical education course every 24 calendar months.

questions.question: Under BasicMed, how often must a pilot have a physical examination?
questions.explanation: BasicMed requires a physical examination by a state-licensed physician every 48 calendar months.

questions.question: What are the aircraft limitations under BasicMed?
options: 6 or fewer seats, 6000 lbs or less MTOW
4 or fewer seats, 3000 lbs or less MTOW
questions.explanation: BasicMed limits operations to aircraft with 6 or fewer seats and 6000 lbs or less maximum certificated takeoff weight.

questions.question: What altitude restriction applies under BasicMed?
questions.explanation: BasicMed limits operations to altitudes below 18,000 feet MSL.

questions.question: What speed restriction applies under BasicMed?
questions.explanation: BasicMed limits operations to speeds not exceeding 250 knots indicated airspeed.

questions.question: Who may NOT use BasicMed?
options: Pilots who have never held a medical certificate
Pilots whose most recent medical was denied, suspended, or revoked
questions.explanation: Pilots whose most recent application was denied, suspended, or revoked may not use BasicMed without obtaining a new medical certificate first.

questions.question: What is required to use BasicMed for the first time?
options: Must have held a valid medical certificate after July 15, 2006
questions.explanation: To use BasicMed, a pilot must have held a valid medical certificate at some point after July 15, 2006.

questions.question: A pilot discovers a medical condition that would disqualify them. What should they do?
options: Continue flying until the medical expires
Immediately stop flying and consult an AME
Only stop flying if symptoms appear
questions.explanation: Per 14 CFR 61.53, a pilot may not act as PIC or required crewmember while knowing of any medical condition that would make them unable to meet medical standards.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of passengers allowed under BasicMed?
options: No passenger limit (aircraft seat limit applies)
questions.explanation: BasicMed limits to aircraft with 6 or fewer seats, so maximum 5 passengers (6 seats minus pilot).

questions.question: Which operations are prohibited under BasicMed?
questions.explanation: BasicMed may not be used for operations requiring a medical certificate for compensation or hire.

questions.question: What color vision standard applies to third class medical?
questions.explanation: Third class medical requires ability to perceive colors necessary for safe performance of airman duties.

questions.question: What happens if a pilot fails the color vision test during a medical exam?
options: Limitation may be placed on certificate
questions.explanation: A limitation such as 'Not valid for night flying or by color signal control' may be placed on the medical certificate.

questions.question: When does a medical certificate expire?
options: At the end of the month shown
At midnight on the date shown
questions.explanation: Medical certificates expire at the end of the month shown on the certificate.

questions.question: What is a Special Issuance medical certificate?
options: A medical issued with conditions for pilots who don't meet standard requirements
A medical for student pilots only
questions.explanation: A Special Issuance (SI) is a medical certificate issued to pilots who don't meet standard requirements but can demonstrate they can safely perform pilot duties.

questions.question: Who issues medical certificates?
options: Aviation Medical Examiners (AMEs) designated by the FAA
questions.explanation: Medical certificates are issued by Aviation Medical Examiners (AMEs) who are physicians designated by the FAA.

questions.question: A first class medical certificate for a pilot age 40 or older is valid for first class privileges for:
questions.explanation: For pilots 40 or older, first class privileges last only 6 calendar months, then the certificate becomes second class.

questions.question: Can a pilot fly with a known medical deficiency?
options: Yes, as long as the medical certificate is current
No, a pilot may not act as PIC knowing of any condition that would make them unable to meet medical standards
Yes, if they feel capable of flying
questions.explanation: Per 14 CFR 61.53, no person may act as PIC or required crewmember knowing of any medical condition that would make them unable to meet requirements for their medical certificate.

questions.question: What is the hearing standard for a third class medical?
options: Demonstrate hearing of average conversational voice at 6 feet
questions.explanation: Third class medical requires demonstration of hearing an average conversational voice in a quiet room at 6 feet, with back turned to examiner.
